1) Primary ask: We need a documented workflow for Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests that covers deletion from primary storage, logging systems, and backups. Our GDPR and customer contracts require erasure from "live" systems within 30 days of a validated request.

2) Backups: We understand that immutable backups can be retained for a period, but we need a clear policy on maximum time to make data unrecoverable (e.g., key destruction, targeted purge, or retention window). What is Redwood's typical bake-to-unrecoverable timeline for backups after a request?

4) Proof-of-deletion: Our auditors will expect an auditable confirmation (timestamped) per deletion request. Do you provide deletion confirmation artifacts?

Jordan - thanks for laying this out so clearly. Follow-up with the short workflow below and a proposed SLA. I'm attaching a one-page workflow and our SOC2 summary for context.

High-level RTBF workflow (summary):
- Request intake: customer submits RTBF via Support portal / API -> ticket created and validated by FinTechCo (ownership of data subject verification).
- Primary deletion: Our platform marks primary records for deletion, runs targeted purge, and removes PII from active databases. Target SLA: 30 calendar days from validated request.
- Logs & telemetry: Standard request logs are retained for operational/monitoring purposes. We support configurable log redaction; sensitive fields can be redacted at ingestion. By default, request/response metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model used) are retained for 1 year; full payloads are retained only if enabled by customer. Logs are included in RTBF only when they contain PII and when redaction is not possible.
- Backups: We keep regular backups per customer retention policy. For immutable/long-term backups, we offer two approaches: (A) key destruction (crypto-erase) to render backups unrecoverable (timeline dependent on backup cadence; typical target: within 90 days), or (B) targeted purge where possible for storage systems that support object-level deletions. We will work with your infra to choose the approach that meets your legal needs.
- Proof-of-deletion: We provide a deletion confirmation package (timestamped report with IDs and artifacts) once primary deletion completes and again when backups are rendered unrecoverable (if using key destruction).

Proposed SLA (example):
- Primary storage deletion: 30 calendar days after validated request.
- Backup unrecoverability (via key destruction): 90 calendar days maximum.
- Logs: configurable; if customer requires full log purge, timeline aligns with backup/unrecoverability window unless logs are stored in active systems that can be purged earlier.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will circulate a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the SLA and owners.
2) Aditya (cc'd) will scope the implementation details (API endpoints, redaction controls, confirmation artifacts).
3) Marissa will work with CS to map your deletion intake process and any data classification we need.

Hi Priya / team - looping in some technical detail on the API and artifacts. Short answers first: yes, programmatic support exists and we can produce the artifacts you requested. Details below.

API / programmatic intake:
- DELETE /v1/customers/{customer_id}/data - endpoint exists in our management API. It requires a validated ticket id and verification metadata. We rate-limit to prevent abuse; typical processing is async with a request id returned and progress webhooks available.

Primary deletion:
- Target 30 calendar days. The API initiates a targeted purge of active stores (Postgres, object store index) and triggers downstream removal of related indices/cache. We return a deletion_report JSON object (request_id, timestamp, list_of_deleted_keys/ids, hashes) that can be archived by FinTechCo.

Backups / unrecoverability:
- Crypto-erase workflow: we can schedule key destruction for customer-specific backup keys. Once keys are destroyed, we produce a crypto-erase certificate (signed) with timestamp, key id, and irreversible-flag. Because of backup cadence, the maximum window to irrecoverability is tied to last backup cycle + key-destruction processing - we currently guarantee a max of 90 days for production accounts under the Dedicated plan; for Hosted customers we can negotiate similar terms under a contractual addendum.

Logs & artifacts:
- Deletion confirmation package includes: deletion_report JSON (primary), crypto-erase_certificate.pdf (if key destruction), and log_redaction_summary.csv (listing log buckets/keys and redaction status).

Caveats / constraints:
- For third-party backups (customer-managed or cloud provider snapshots we don't control), we can coordinate but cannot guarantee purge; the MAP should document ownership.
- Immutable long-term archives that are subject to legal hold will override RTBF until hold is lifted. The MAP should include an escalation path for legal holds.

I'll take point on producing a MAP draft that includes the artifacts list; Camila - I'll attach the draft MAP and proposed API spec for review.
